# twi-mirror-paths.txt — the extraction contract for the TWI Research Center mirror.
#
# Why this file exists. github.com/simonpsson/twi-research-center is a
# HISTORY-PRESERVING extraction of the TWI subset of this repository, produced by
# git-filter-repo reading exactly this file (see scripts/twi-mirror-sync.mjs).
# Until this file existed the path list lived only in a gitignored working ledger,
# which made the mirror unreproducible by anyone but the session that built it:
# the same 60 commits could only be regenerated by remembering the argument list.
#
# The list is LOAD-BEARING in a way that is easy to miss. filter-repo output is
# deterministic — same history plus same paths gives byte-identical commit SHAs —
# so this file is what makes each sync a fast-forward instead of a history
# rewrite. Editing an entry changes every tree that entry touches, cascades into
# every descendant commit hash, and turns the next sync into a non-fast-forward
# push that scripts/twi-mirror-sync.mjs will refuse. Add entries freely; changing
# or removing one is a republish of the mirror's whole history.
#
# Entries are filter-repo --paths-from-file syntax: a bare line is a literal path
# or directory prefix, `glob:` introduces a glob. A trailing slash matters —
# `twi/` is the built bundle directory, and without the slash it would also drag
# in twi-migration-001-creation-core.sql by prefix.
#
# Coverage is not trusted to this file alone. twi-mirror-sync.mjs re-derives the
# set of TWI-owned paths from the source tree on every run and FAILS if one is not
# covered here, because an enumerated allowlist decays silently — this project has
# already been bitten once by exactly that (a contract check that passed only
# because its enumerated file list had not grown with the code).

# --- the application, its tests, and the built bundle Pages actually serves ---
src/twi/
functions/api/twi/
twi/
twi-migration-001-creation-core.sql

# --- build and test configuration owned by TWI ---
tsconfig.twi.json
vite.twi.config.ts
vitest.twi.config.ts

# --- the orchestrator Worker: its own package, its own toolchain ---
# A separate sub-package with wrangler 4 and workers-types 5, deliberately not the root's
# wrangler 3. Every path under it contains "twi", so the sync's coverage check refuses to
# publish until this entry exists -- that refusal is the mechanism working, not an
# obstacle. The trailing slash matters here for the same reason it does on `twi/`.
twi-orchestrator/

# TWI's finishing helpers and their tests. The rest of stems-gpu/ is Stem Lab's and stays
# out: app.py and registry.py serve a different product that happens to share the Modal app.
stems-gpu/finish.py
stems-gpu/test_finish.py

# --- the guards: TWI-named scripts, plus the two shared libraries they need ---
glob:scripts/twi-*
glob:scripts/lib/twi-*
scripts/lib/functions-registry.mjs
scripts/lib/ts-ast.mjs

# --- the documents that make the extraction legible on its own ---
# Deliberately NOT all of docs/superpowers/: that tree holds unrelated projects'
# plans and specs, and a first extraction attempt leaked six of them.
docs/superpowers/HANDOVER.md
docs/superpowers/TASK8-CLAUDE-CODE-HANDOFF.md
docs/superpowers/TASK11-HANDOFF.md
docs/superpowers/TWI-AUDIO-AI-DEEP-RESEARCH-2026-08-30.md
docs/superpowers/mutants/README.md
docs/superpowers/mutants/twi-creation-core.mutants.json
glob:docs/superpowers/mutants/harnesses/*
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-16-twi-creation-core.md
docs/superpowers/research/report-source.md
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-16-twi-research-center-design.md
